what_it_does: When engineers redesign or optimize a digital circuit — say, to make it faster or cheaper — they need to prove that the new version behaves identically to the original. This is called equivalence checking, and when the two circuits do not tick through their states at the same rate (called non-cycle-accurate designs), the proof requires finding a mathematical relationship, called a refinement relation, that maps states in one circuit to states in the other. Finding these mappings by hand is tedious and requires deep expertise in formal methods. This paper presents an algorithm that automatically discovers compact, human-readable refinement relations between two such circuits using a technique called relational mapping abstraction — essentially, it searches for the simplest symbolic description that proves the two designs always produce the same outputs. The work aims to make formal verification of chip transformations more accessible and less error-prone.
